audits.title: A perinatal audit of neonatal deaths in three Danish counties.
audits.standard: Generally accepted standards of satisfactory perinatal and neonatal care
audits.setting: Three Danish counties (A, B and C)

cycle1.result: County without a neonatal intensive care unit had significantly more potentially avoidable deaths than the county with a fully staffed NICU; suboptimal care in another county linked to inadequate staffing and inexperienced junior doctors.

audits.other_findings: Fewer liveborn infants under 28 weeks were reported to the Birth Register in the county without a NICU.
audits.citation: Andersen KV, Lange AP, Helweg-Larsen K, Andersen E. A perinatal audit of neonatal deaths in three Danish counties. Dan Med Bull. 1991;38(4):382-385. PMID: 1914538.

audits.title: Prospective Audit of Avoidable Factors in Institutional Stillbirths and Early Neonatal Deaths at Tikur Anbessa Hospital in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
audits.setting: Labour room and NICU, Tikur Anbessa Hospital, Addis Ababa

cycle1.result: 30 stillbirths and 31 early neonatal deaths among 1,225 deliveries (PMR 50/1,000); avoidable factors in 70% of deaths, 84% of them health worker-related.

audits.intervention: Quality improvement programmes targeting identified gaps being implemented.
audits.other_findings: Patient-related factors 11% and administrative factors 5% of avoidable factors.
audits.citation: Demise A, Gebrehiwot Y, Worku B, Spector JM. Prospective Audit of Avoidable Factors in Institutional Stillbirths and Early Neonatal Deaths at Tikur Anbessa Hospital in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Afr J Reprod Health. 2015;19(4):78-86. PMID: 27337856.

audits.title: Lessons learned in cases of late preterm mortality in the Netherlands: Results from nationwide perinatal audits, a mixed method study.
audits.standard: Nationwide perinatal audit theme of late preterm mortality (32+0 to 36+6 weeks), identifying improvable care factors
audits.setting: Local perinatal cooperation units, nationwide perinatal audit

cycle1.result: 52 improvable care factors identified, mostly inadequate CTG fetal monitoring in labour, unclear local responsibilities and work procedures, and poor communication at transfer of care

audits.other_findings: Case-review (confidential enquiry-style) audit rather than measurement against a numerical target.
audits.citation: Baauw L, Rosman AN, van den Akker TH. Lessons learned in cases of late preterm mortality in the Netherlands: Results from nationwide perinatal audits, a mixed method study. Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol X. 2023;17:100179. doi:10.1016/j.eurox.2023.100179. PMID: 36824398.

audits.title: Quality in neonatal mortality audits: Results of pilot study from district of Dhule, Maharashtra.
audits.standard: WHO modified checklist for quality in audit toolkit
audits.setting: Health facilities in Dhule district, Maharashtra

cycle1.result: Almost half of members were not told the vision and framework of audit; secondary care hospitals lacked accuracy and consistency in audit documentation.

audits.other_findings: 25 healthcare workers interviewed; an SOP for audit committees is recommended.
audits.citation: Pande BS, Patel AR, Patil AJ, Patel S, Shaikh MU. Quality in neonatal mortality audits: Results of pilot study from district of Dhule, Maharashtra. J Family Med Prim Care. 2023;12(9):2032-2035. doi:10.4103/jfmpc.jfmpc_178_23. PMID: 38024895.

audits.title: Suboptimal factors in maternal and newborn care for refugees: Lessons learned from perinatal audits in the Netherlands.
audits.standard: National perinatal audit identifying suboptimal factors in care (Three Delays Model)

cycle1.result: 29 suboptimal factors identified; all 53 cases contained suboptimal factors; in 67.9% at least one most likely or probably contributed to the adverse outcome

audits.other_findings: Factors were 7 care-seeking, 6 accessibility and 16 quality of care; focuses on refugee women.
audits.citation: Verschuuren AEH, Tankink JB, Postma IR, Bergman KA, Goodarzi B, Feijen-de Jong EI, et al.. Suboptimal factors in maternal and newborn care for refugees: Lessons learned from perinatal audits in the Netherlands. PLoS One. 2024;19(6):e0305764. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0305764. PMID: 38935661.

audits.title: Preventability and contributing factors in neonatal deaths in protracted refugee camp settings: A five-year audit among Syrian refugees in Jordan.
audits.standard: Three Delays taxonomy and preventability adjudication

cycle1.result: Concurrent Delay 1 and 3 factors in 164 deaths (92.7%); suboptimal ANC in 70.6%; poor high-risk pregnancy management in 57.6%; clinician non-adherence to standards in 46.3%; 41.8% definitely and 33.9% probably preventable.

audits.other_findings: 99.4% of mothers received antenatal care despite frequent quality deficiencies.
audits.citation: Shtaiyat I, Khader Y, Fawad M, Al Nsour M, Abu Khadair M. Preventability and contributing factors in neonatal deaths in protracted refugee camp settings: A five-year audit among Syrian refugees in Jordan. J Neonatal Perinatal Med. 2026. doi:10.1177/19345798261489879. PMID: 42749272.

audits.title: Impact of Action Taken in Response to Stillbirth Audit: A Success Story.
audits.setting: Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Lady Hardinge Medical College, New Delhi
audits.intervention: Ultrasound at 34-36 weeks' gestation and intrapartum monitoring on a common customised labour chart for all providers (POCQI methodology).
audits.other_findings: Intra-facility failure to identify FGR fell significantly (p=0.033; RR 0.37), and inadequate monitoring as a provider cause declined.
audits.citation: Kumar M, Puri M, Suka M, Chawla N, Kaur GP, Yadav R, et al.. Impact of Action Taken in Response to Stillbirth Audit: A Success Story. J Obstet Gynaecol India. 2023;73(Suppl 1):61-68. doi:10.1007/s13224-023-01808-1. PMID: 37916007.

audits.title: Confidential Audit of Perinatal Mortality in the Republic of Kazakhstan: A Pilot Study.
audits.standard: Confidential audit grading of care quality (categories of substandard care)

cycle1.result: 93% of cases fell into categories of substandard or potentially inadequate care (categories 2 and 3); 34 antenatal, 6 intranatal and 76 early neonatal deaths.

audits.other_findings: Intraventricular haemorrhage and sepsis were leading causes of neonatal death; maternal comorbidity and insufficient antenatal visits linked to antenatal and intranatal deaths.
audits.citation: Marat A, Khamidullina Z, Muratbekova S, Jaxalykova K, Karin B, Samatova N, et al.. Confidential Audit of Perinatal Mortality in the Republic of Kazakhstan: A Pilot Study. Med Sci (Basel). 2025;13(2):77. doi:10.3390/medsci13020077. PMID: 40559235.

audits.title: Perinatal Deaths in Suriname: A Nationwide Cohort Study on Causes of Death and Lessons Learned from Facility-Based Audits.
audits.standard: WHO Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response cycle
audits.setting: Nationwide facility-based perinatal death surveillance and audit (MPDSR)

cycle1.result: 83 stillbirths and 72 neonatal deaths; PMR 28.2 per 1000 total births; 63 audited cases had 150 modifiable factors, half related to quality of care.

audits.other_findings: Suboptimal antenatal care, substandard neonatal life support, delays in seeking care and shortages of supplies and staff contributed; 49% of antepartum stillbirths had unknown cause.
audits.citation: Prüst ZD, Verschueren KJC, Liesdek S, Rigters F, Bhika-Kori G, Bloemenkamp KWM, et al.. Perinatal Deaths in Suriname: A Nationwide Cohort Study on Causes of Death and Lessons Learned from Facility-Based Audits. Matern Child Health J. 2026;30(6):843-854. doi:10.1007/s10995-026-04280-1. PMID: 42133245.

audits.title: Audit cycle improves the quality of assistance in the management of stillbirth: A 10 years' experience.
audits.standard: Quality of assistance in stillbirth management (audit cycle with preventability assessment)
audits.intervention: Audit cycle implemented at local and central levels.
audits.other_findings: 1041 stillbirths overall (rate 0.33%); maternal conditions as cause (OR 0.34) and unexplained cases (OR 0.62) fell.
audits.citation: Monari F, Benuzzi M, Costantini RC, Guariglia G, Melis B, Neri I, et al.. Audit cycle improves the quality of assistance in the management of stillbirth: A 10 years' experience. Pregnancy (Hoboken). 2025;1(6):e70141. doi:10.1002/pmf2.70141. PMID: 42597128.
